verifications.claim: As of early April 2026, over 3.1 million bottles of various eye drops have been voluntarily recalled by K.C. Pharmaceuticals.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "3.1 million bottles... voluntarily recalled... by K.C. Pharmaceuticals" (R1); "3,111,072 bottles... voluntarily recalled... KC Pharmaceuticals" (R2); similar in R3-R8
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the recall by K.C. Pharmaceuticals of over 3.1 million bottles, with articles dated early April 2026.

verifications.claim: The recall by K.C. Pharmaceuticals is due to potential lack of assurance of sterility.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lack of assurance of sterility" (R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly states the reason as 'lack of assurance of sterility'.

verifications.claim: The recalled products were sold at CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Walmart, and H-E-B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, H-E-B (R1-R8); Walmart (R8: "H-E-B, Walgreens, Walmart and CVS")
verifications.reasoning: All listed retailers are confirmed across multiple references as selling the recalled products.

verifications.claim: The recalled products include various Dry Eye Relief and Artificial Tears products.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Dry Eye Relief Eye Drops"; "Artificial Tears Sterile Lubricant Eye Drops" (R1-R7)
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly list 'Dry Eye Relief' and 'Artificial Tears' among the recalled products.

verifications.claim: Brands affected by the recall include Best Choice, Careone, CVS Health, Equaline, Foster & Thrive, Good Neighbor Pharmacy, H-E-B, Leader, Major, Meijer, QC-Quality Choice, Rite Aid, TopCare Health, and Walgreens.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: Best Choice, Careone/CareOne, CVS Health, Equaline, Foster & Thrive, Good Neighbor Pharmacy, H-E-B, Leader, Meijer, QC-Quality Choice, Rite Aid, TopCare Health, Walgreens listed (R3, R4); no mention of "Major" in any reference
verifications.reasoning: All brands except 'Major' are directly supported; 'Major' is not mentioned in any source, making the full list incorrect.

verifications.claim: The recall includes products with expiration dates ranging from April 30 to July 31, 2026.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "expiration dates ranging from April 30 to July 31, 2026" (R1); "expiration dates ranging from April to October... AR24M01, Oct. 31; LT24M01, Oct. 31" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: R1 supports the exact range; R3 contradicts by listing products expiring up to October 31, indicating a broader range.

verifications.claim: The FDA classified this as a Class II recall.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Class II recall" or "Class II designation" (R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state FDA classified it as Class II recall.

verifications.claim: No injuries or infections have been reported to date.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "no one has reported an infection" (R1); "There aren’t reports of injuries" (R6); "not clear if there have been any reports of adverse effects" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm no reports of injuries or infections; no contradictions.
